flashcards.back: One unbroken loop of components joined by wires, around which charge flows; break the loop anywhere and the flow stops everywhere.
The flow of charge around the loop, measured in amps by an ammeter; in a series loop it is the same at every point.
The agreed direction of current flow: out of the battery's positive terminal, around the loop, and back into the negative terminal.
An arrangement with only one path for the charge, so every component carries the same current and one break stops everything.
An arrangement where each component sits on its own branch, so one can fail while the others keep working.
How much a component opposes the current, measured in ohms; in Ohm's law, V = I R, a fixed 4 ohm resistance lets 12 volts drive 3 amps.
The relation V = I R between voltage, current and resistance: with resistance fixed, doubling the voltage doubles the current.
The unit of current: the series loop in the animation carries 0.5 amps, read the same on both sides of the bulb.

The bulb glows and gets hot, so it looks like it consumes the electricity flowing through it. Current is not used up: an ammeter reads the same 0.5 amps on both sides of the bulb. In class, place the ammeter on each side of the bulb in turn: 0.5 A before, 0.5 A after - the bulb changed electrical energy into light and heat, but no current disappeared.
flashcards.front: The bulb uses up the current.

flashcards.back: Wrong - the second ammeter also reads 0.5 A, because current is not used up in a series loop
flashcards.front: In a series circuit an ammeter before a bulb reads 0.5 A. A classmate says the ammeter after the bulb must read less, because the bulb has used some current up. Which statement is correct?
A 12 V battery is connected across a resistor of 4 ohms. Calculate the current, showing the Ohm's law step.

items.answer: Wrong - the second ammeter also reads 0.5 A, because current is not used up in a series loop
items.prompt: In a series circuit an ammeter before a bulb reads 0.5 A. A classmate says the ammeter after the bulb must read less, because the bulb has used some current up. Which statement is correct?
A 12 V battery is connected across a resistor of 4 ohms. Calculate the current, showing the Ohm's law step.

items.answer: Exactly 0.5 A - current is the same all around a series loop
items.prompt: An ammeter reads 0.5 A just before a bulb in a series circuit. What does an ammeter just after the bulb read?

items.answer: It stays lit, because it sits on its own branch with a complete path
